newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rights group accuses Algerian state of grave abuses.
newsitem.headline: Rights group accuses Algerian state of grave abuses.

text.p: A human rights group accused Algerian security forces on Tuesday of resorting to summary executions, kidnappings and torture in their fight against Moslem guerrillas.

A mission of the Paris-based International Federation of Human Rights (FIDH), which visited Algeria for six days last month, said that at least two thousand people had disappeared at the hands of state security forces.
It said the authorities in some cases preferred to kill suspects rather than hand them over to justice officials, and a state-armed militia were responsible for killings and massacres.
FIDH said Algeria's five-year-old war between Islamist guerrillas and the government may have cost 100,000 lives.

Some 60,000 people are generally estimated to have died in political violence since Algeria's military-backed authorities in January 1992 scrapped an election which the radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) was poised to win.
Bomb attacks and massacres blamed on Islamist guerrillas have flared up recently, an apparent attempt to dissuade voters from taking part in parliamentary elections scheduled for Thursday.
The FIDH mission said it went to Algeria to investigate the functioning of justice but "was confronted with overwhelming extra-judiciary phenomena".
It said that while authorities, "in talks marked with concealment and lies, were satisfied with admitting a few 'abuses'", there was evidence of systematic and widespread human rights violations.

It said suspects were being arrested by plainclothes police without warrants and held secretly and illegally for long periods in army or paramilitary gendarmerie barracks, or in police stations which the authorities did not recognise as detention centres.

Citing testimony from a variety of witnesses, it said torture was widespread and included beatings, whipping, sodomy, choking, burns and -- in two reported cases -- the use of blow torches on genitals.
Relatives were also being tortured in order to force suspects to confess, the group said.
It quoted the Algerian National Human Rights Organisation as saying that many people had disappeared.
That group said some had been kidnapped by security forces or Moslem guerrillas while others had joined the Islamists, or gone into hiding to escape the army draft.
The FIDH mission estimated that at least 2,000 of the disappearances could be blamed on the Algerian security forces but said the actual number was probably far higher.
"FIDH can state that Algerian authorities cannot ignore the scope of the disappearances," it said.
The group said that while Moslem guerrillas were carrying out horrific massacres, village militias were also responsible for massacres officially blamed on the guerrillas.
FIDH said that while it recognised Algeria's duty to fight the guerrillas, "it considers that the authorities and security forces must not respond with crimes to the terrorists' crimes".
